plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A hardy perennial prized for dense, layered blooms in many forms, from pompons to spiders. It is one of the last major garden flowers to bloom in the Northern Hemisphere, thriving in cool autumn temperatures and short days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter (October to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated in East Asia, Europe, and North America; native to China
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are a photoperiodic short-day plant, and in Japan the Chrysanthemum Festival honors the flower, which is also the emblem of the Imperial family.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, semi-deciduous tree that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In late spring the blooms carpet streets and gardens with purple petals across the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Argentina and Bolivia; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Brazil, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, there are tens of thousands of jacarandas, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'. Australian students traditionally say that if a jacaranda blossom falls on your head, you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves that produces delicate, often lightly fragrant flowers in autumn, earlier than most other camellias. It is common in gardens and hedges in mild climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, used in Japan for cooking, cosmetics, and hair care.

plants.name: Cyclamen hederifolium
plants.description: A small woodland tuberous perennial whose swept-back pink flowers appear before the marbled, ivy-shaped leaves. It naturalizes beneath trees and shrubs and brings color to the autumn forest floor.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to late autumn (September to November)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean region and southern Europe through Turkey; naturalized in the UK and parts of North America
plants.funFact: After flowering, the flower stalks coil like springs and pull the seed capsules to the ground, where ants help disperse the seeds.
